bottleneck.description: US launch and space-services company (Alpha small-lift, Blue Ghost lunar lander, Elytra orbital transfer, Eclipse medium-lift with Northrop Grumman); the first commercial operator to complete a fully successful lunar soft landing.

dependency.key_customers: NASA (CLPS), US Space Force, US Department of Defense / DIU, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman

editorial.notes: Firefly's one distinctive asset is being the only commercial entity with a proven, fully successful lunar landing (Blue Ghost, March 2025), and it is the sole-source domestic first-stage supplier for Northrop Grumman's Antares 330 and Eclipse. Both are real, but neither is route-around-proof: NASA deliberately multi-sources lunar delivery through CLPS, and the Alpha launch business is openly contested by Rocket Lab and SpaceX rideshare with a mixed reliability record. The deepest dependency actually runs the wrong way, with a heavily concentrated US-government customer base. Niche leadership with real switching costs rather than a choke point, so MEDIUM, on the Rocket Lab calibration. Engines and stages are built in-house; no external supplier is disclosed at a sourceable level.
